# Platform Support Model

<!-- Generated by scripts/check_platforms.py from project/platforms.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

This is the target-engine (Rust) platform capability matrix - what this repository's own CI and test suite actually verify today, not an aspiration. `tier: 1` means real, CI-verified identity **and** mutation (deletion) capability; `tier: 2` means the platform is a named target but has not yet met that bar for at least one capability. See `docs/architecture/PLATFORM_MODEL.md` for the underlying capability seams (`IdentityObserver`, `MutationExecutor`, ...) each row's `identity`/`mutation` column refers to.

| Platform | Tier | CI (check) | CI (quality) | Identity | Mutation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel) | 1 | yes | yes | verified | verified |
| Linux (x86_64, glibc) | 1 | yes | yes | verified | verified |
| Windows native (x86_64) | 2 | yes | yes | verified | unsupported |
| WSL2 (Windows host, Linux guest) | 2 | no | no | unverified | unverified |

## macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel)

Full CI (check + quality: fmt/clippy/test/cargo-deny) on macos-latest. Real identity (device/inode, E03-S01) and real, adversarially-tested deletion (E03-S05/E21-S07) are both verified on this platform's own CI.

Evidence (real test functions in `rust/crates/`):

- `toctou_file_deleted_and_recreated_with_identical_content_still_changes_identity`
- `establish_rejects_a_root_swapped_to_a_symlink_after_final_validation_but_before_the_bind`

## Linux (x86_64, glibc)

Same Unix code path and same tests as macOS, run on its own ubuntu-latest CI - not assumed identical from macOS's result alone. E07-S05 found and fixed a real Linux-specific timing divergence (inode reuse on same-second delete-recreate) that macOS CI alone had never surfaced, which is why this platform is verified independently rather than inferred from macOS.

Evidence (real test functions in `rust/crates/`):

- `toctou_file_deleted_and_recreated_with_identical_content_still_changes_identity`
- `establish_rejects_a_root_swapped_to_a_symlink_after_final_validation_but_before_the_bind`

## Windows native (x86_64)

Full CI exists and real file/volume identity + reparse-point classification is implemented and verified there (E20-S01, ADR-0020). Real deletion is not: `cancellai-platform::mutation::confirmed_delete_file`'s cfg(not(unix)) arm and `cancellai-sealedfs::SealedRoot`'s no-follow root-establishment walk both refuse unconditionally on Windows today, so `clean` is inspect-only there. Tier 1 requires this repository's own bar for what this product does (safe, verified deletion), not merely CI presence - remains tier 2 until a future story implements and verifies it.

Evidence (real test functions in `rust/crates/`):

- `observe_identity_reports_is_reparse_point_for_a_real_symlink_without_following_it`
- `observe_identity_two_hardlinks_to_the_same_file_share_a_file_index`

## WSL2 (Windows host, Linux guest)

No dedicated CI runner exists for WSL2 in this repository (GitHub Actions has no WSL2 runner image). A WSL2 guest is a real Linux kernel, so the same Unix identity/mutation code path that is verified on Linux would very likely work there too - but that is an inference, not this repository's own evidence, so it is disclosed as unverified rather than silently inherited from Linux's tier. E20-S02 added explicit WSL2/`/mnt` detection (RuntimeEnvironment, FilesystemContext), itself also unverified against a real WSL2 guest for the same reason.

Evidence: none yet - disclosed, not silently assumed from another platform.

## Tier 2, further out

- SSH remote hosts.
- Dev Containers.
- Ephemeral CI runners.
- Codespaces-like developer environments.

None of these are named platforms above because none has begun implementation; they are recorded here as acknowledged future scope, not as a claim about current behavior.

## Unsupported consumer platforms

Mobile operating systems are not a product target. cancellAI governs development machines and development execution environments.

## What a non-tier-1 platform does today

Unsupported/tier-2 mutation capability never means an unverified guess at deletion. `cancellai-platform`'s observers (`IdentityObserver`, `AllocationObserver`, ...) report a distinct `Unsupported` fact rather than a possibly-wrong result, and the safety kernel (`cancellai-safety::root_capability`, `cancellai-safety::mutation_executor`) fails closed on it (SI-002, SI-017) - inspection/planning commands remain available, but `clean` cannot proceed to a real deletion. This is explicit refusal, not silent partial behavior (`docs/architecture/PLATFORM_MODEL.md`).

## Cross-platform rule

The domain layer does not expose Unix-only identity assumptions. Platform implementations must provide capability-aware abstractions for:

- filesystem object identity;
- volume/filesystem boundary;
- symbolic links, junctions, mount points, and reparse points;
- allocated/reclaimable size estimation;
- process/activity observation;
- atomic rename/move guarantees;
- user-service runtime;
- notifications;
- path normalization and case behavior.
